integrity: The proof starts from the published exact quasi-metric and polar description, computes all facet and vertex radii in the inherited zero-sum metric, proves strict shell ordering algebraically, certifies the Lipschitz inradius and uniqueness by summing the nearest directed-cycle facets, and certifies the polar minimum-enclosing sphere and uniqueness by the zero barycenter of the outer vertex cycle. Finite verification is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the explicit clock-quasi-metric Lipschitz/Kantorovich--Rubinstein polar pair in the standard zero-sum Euclidean realization. It is not a metric invariant of the combinatorial cyclohedron and does not determine the opposite radius problem for either member of the polar pair. A broader theorem for cyclic quasi-metrics under different terminology remains a residual originality risk.
title: Clock distance gives reciprocal Euclidean radii for the cyclohedral Lipschitz–KR pair
